name: speedy (binary serialization)
verdict_reason: The speed holds: in the 2026-08-07 run speedy 0.8.7 serialized 3.0x-34x and deserialized 1.10x-25.7x faster than bincode 1.3.3. But it has had no commit since 2024-10 or release since 2024-01, the benchmark removed it as unmaintained later that month, and wincode now posts similar numbers while staying bincode-compatible.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark with public code; rustc nightly, the CPU and lto = true are stated.
claimed_speedup: Serialize 153.12 µs vs 464.75 µs (log), 141.52 µs vs 4.8569 ms (mesh), 165.88 µs vs 518.86 µs (minecraft_savedata); deserialize 1.3994 ms vs 1.6158 ms, 141.74 µs vs 3.6395 ms, 1.3890 ms vs 1.5229 ms; 3.0x-34x serialize, 1.10x-25.7x deserialize (ratios derived from page data)
workload: rust_serialization_benchmark log, mesh and minecraft_savedata datasets with speedy's own Readable/Writable derives (little-endian context).
toolchain: rustc 1.99.0-nightly (2026-08-06), bench profile lto = true, no target-cpu flag
one_liner: Fast custom-derive binary serializer, 3x-34x faster than bincode 1.3 to serialize, but unmaintained and dropped from the main benchmark.
how_it_is_fast: Its own Readable/Writable derives read and write fields directly against a fixed endianness context, with no serde Serializer or Visitor layer in between.
use_it_when: Existing code already on speedy that needs no new features
skip_it_when: New projects: pick wincode (bincode-compatible) or bitcode, which are maintained and post similar or better numbers
You need fixes or new type support; the repository has been quiet since 2024-10
caveats: Last measured 2026-08-07; rust_serialization_benchmark deleted its speedy harness in the 2026-08 cleanup under its unmaintained-crate policy
tradeoffs: Speedy's own format; not compatible with bincode or serde formats

evidence.quote: The goal of this crate is to provide fast, simple and easy binary serialization.
Unmaintained crates are subject to removal from the benchmarks.
